sections.t: A contract requires mutual assent: an offer inviting acceptance, and an acceptance mirroring its terms.
A promise is enforceable when supported by bargained-for exchange.
Detrimental reliance can substitute for consideration under promissory estoppel.

nodes.title: Lucy v. Zehmer
nodes.desc: Objective theory of assent: a drunken 'joke' offer to sell a farm, written and signed, binds when a reasonable person would take it seriously.

sections.t: Zehmer, drinking with Lucy, wrote and signed an agreement to sell his farm for $50,000, later claiming it was a joke.
Outward expressions control over secret intent; the contract was enforceable.
Mutual assent is judged objectively, by what a reasonable person would understand.

nodes.title: Carlill v. Carbolic Smoke Ball
nodes.desc: A newspaper advertisement promising £100 to anyone who used the smoke ball and caught influenza was a unilateral offer accepted by performance.

sections.t: The company advertised a £100 reward and deposited £1,000 to show sincerity; Mrs. Carlill used the ball and caught flu.
The advertisement was an offer to the world, accepted by performance of the conditions.

nodes.title: Hamer v. Sidway
nodes.desc: An uncle's promise of $5,000 if his nephew abstained from drinking, tobacco, and gambling until 21 was supported by consideration: forbearance of a legal right.

sections.t: Waiver of any legal right at the request of another is sufficient consideration.
Consideration may be a benefit to the promisor or a detriment to the promisee.

nodes.title: Kirksey v. Kirksey
nodes.desc: A brother-in-law's invitation to 'come see me' with land to cultivate was a mere gratuitous promise; moving one's household was a condition, not consideration.

sections.t: A gratuitous promise is unenforceable even when the promisee incurs inconvenience relying on it.

nodes.title: Ricketts v. Scothorn
nodes.desc: A grandfather's note so his granddaughter 'would not have to work' became enforceable when she quit her job in reliance — equitable estoppel fills the consideration gap.

sections.t: Intentional influence followed by reasonable reliance estops the promisor from pleading lack of consideration.

nodes.title: Feinberg v. Pfeiffer Co.
nodes.desc: A promised pension induced retirement; past service was not consideration, but retirement in reliance made the promise enforceable under promissory estoppel.

sections.t: Reliance on a pension promise, by retiring and forgoing employment, substitutes for consideration.
